1	---
2	name: kg
3	category: knowledge
4	description: "Load relevant entities from the bstack knowledge graph (research/entities/) for a given topic. Two-tier scoring: tier-1 (catalog-only, ~5ms — slug + tags + claim + links + sources match against docs/knowledge-index.md) is the fast first pass and the only stage for high-confidence exact-slug/tag queries; tier-2 (body-grep fallback, ~300ms — auto-fires when tier-1 returns < N matches OR its best hit is below the confidence floor, default 18) recovers topics whose vocabulary appears in entity prose but not the dense catalog (hit rate jumps from 70% → 100% on representative queries; this is hit rate ≥1, not true recall@N). Surfaces top-N entity bodies as a single context block the agent reasons over. This is a LOAD skill, not a query DSL — querying is what the agent does once loaded. Implements the LLM-as-index architecture (BRO-1223): substrate canonical, one projection (catalog) routes, agent IS the query engine. Empirical: peak per-query context drops from 29% → 4.6% of 1M (6.3× reduction); cumulative session tokens 23.8× fewer over 10 queries. Default N=10 entities; override with --n. Tier-2 auto-fires on few-OR-weak tier-1 hits (confidence gate, default --tier2-floor 18; BRO-1426 lifts R@5 0.871→0.952, MRR 0.868→0.968 with no flag); force unconditionally with --body-search, disable the gate with --tier2-floor 0. Routing-quality flags (BRO-1422): --terms (query expansion — score agent-supplied synonyms/variants alongside the topic), --expand 1 (graph 1-hop — also load related: neighbours of top hits, capped at --n extra, total ≤ 2x--n), --explain (per-signal score trace); hub-aware tiebreak always on. Output: catalog header + ranked entity blocks with full body. USE WHEN load knowledge graph, kg load, load entities, route to entities, load context for, what do we know about, what entities are relevant to, surface knowledge on, browse the graph for, find entities about, semantic load, topical load, agent-as-index load. NOT FOR PAI session retrieval (use ContextSearch), web research (use Research), Knowledge Archive ingest (use Knowledge), or entity write/edit operations (those are direct Read+Edit + commit per the AGENTS.md §P6 sub-rule on substrate-edit-as-inference-persistence)."
5	argument-hint: [topic]
6	effort: low
7	---
8	
9	# kg — knowledge graph loader
10	
11	Load relevant entities for: **$ARGUMENTS**
12	
13	## Purpose
14	
15	The bstack knowledge graph lives at `research/entities/**/*.md` (~250 entities, ~1.1 MB, ~280k tokens). It fits in any 1M-context model with 3.5× headroom — meaning the LLM **is** the index. This skill performs the routing step: reads the dense catalog at `docs/knowledge-index.md`, ranks entities by topical relevance, and surfaces the top-N bodies as a single context block.
16	
17	The agent does the rest: traversal, inference, contradiction detection, semantic comparison — all by reading. There is no SQL layer, no embeddings, no typed-edge schema. The substrate is canonical; the catalog routes; the agent reasons.
18	
19	## Usage
20	
21	```
22	/kg load <topic>              # default: top 10 (two-tier; tier-2 auto-fires on few OR weak tier-1 hits)
23	/kg load <topic> --n 20       # widen the load
24	/kg load <topic> --type tool  # restrict by entity type
25	/kg load <topic> --terms "recall,persistence"  # query expansion: score synonyms/variants too
26	/kg load <topic> --expand 1   # also load 1-hop related: neighbours of the top hits
27	/kg load <topic> --explain    # show the per-signal score trace for each loaded entity
28	/kg load <topic> --body-search  # force tier-2 body grep unconditionally
29	/kg load <topic> --tier2-floor 0  # disable the confidence gate (tier-2 only on count<--n)
30	/kg load <topic> --json       # machine-readable output (for piping)
31	/kg                           # catalog-only mode: print summary stats + top hubs
32	```
33	
34	### Routing-quality flags (BRO-1422)
35	
36	These raise routing **recall** without leaving the LLM-as-index architecture
37	(no sidecar, no embeddings). The gap was never reasoning — a frontier agent
38	reranking the top-N already beats a small reranker model — it was that whatever
39	routing drops below N, the agent never sees.
40	
41	- **`--terms` (query expansion).** The single biggest recall lever. The catalog
42	  scorer matches literal terms; pass the synonyms/variants the topic implies and
43	  they're scored alongside it. The agent IS the query expander here — no headless
44	  expansion model needed (that's the only reason QMD fine-tunes one). Repeatable
45	  (one value per flag); each value may be comma/space-separated. Topic terms keep
46	  priority on ties.
47	- **`--expand 1` (graph 1-hop).** After ranking, also pull the `related:`
48	  neighbours of the top hits — the structural advantage flat-document search
49	  (BM25, vector) structurally cannot offer. Automates the "reading frontier"
50	  (Phase 3). Neighbours are deduped against the primary set, ranked by their own
51	  relevance then in-degree, and **capped at `--n` extra entities** (so total load
52	  is ≤ 2×`--n`) — a hub neighbour (e.g. `arcan`, in-degree 100+) can't explode the
53	  load. Each is marked `↳ via <seed>` (its immediate parent). Only 1 hop is
54	  supported for now (values >1 clamp to 1, so `via` provenance always resolves);
55	  under `--type`, expansion is limited to that type (a one-line note is printed)
56	  since cross-type edges aren't resolved.
57	- **`--explain` (score trace).** Prints which signals fired per entity
58	  (`slug==x(+10) tag==y(+4) … = N catalog`, plus a `+M tier-2 body grep`
59	  residual line when the body grep contributed). Use it to debug routing misses.
60	- **hub-aware tiebreak (always on).** At equal relevance, the more-connected
61	  entity (higher catalog in-degree) sorts first instead of alphabetically —
62	  a cheap stand-in for a hub-rank RRF term.
63	
64	## Workflow
65	
66	### Phase 1 — Verify catalog freshness
67	
68	Check `docs/knowledge-index.md` exists and is fresh:
69	
70	```bash
71	ls -la ~/broomva/docs/knowledge-index.md
72	head -5 ~/broomva/docs/knowledge-index.md  # check `generated:` timestamp
73	```
74	
75	If the catalog is older than the Stop hook's regeneration cadence (~24h), regenerate first:
76	
77	```bash
78	python3 ~/broomva/skills/bookkeeping/scripts/bookkeeping.py index
79	```
80	
81	### Phase 2 — Load relevant entities (two-tier scoring)
82	
83	Run the loader against the user's topic:
84	
85	```bash
86	python3 ~/.claude/skills/kg/scripts/kg.py load "$ARGUMENTS"
87	```
88	
89	The loader uses two tiers:
90	
91	**Tier 1 — catalog-only (fast, ~5ms)**
92	1. Parses the catalog into per-entity blocks
93	2. Scores against catalog metadata only:
94	   - exact slug match: +10
95	   - exact alias match: +8  (BRO-1423 — `aka:` alternate names: kepano synonyms + merged-away dup slugs; querying an alias routes to the canonical)
96	   - slug substring: +5
97	   - alias substring: +4
98	   - tag exact: +4
99	   - tag substring: +3
100	   - claim substring: +3
101	   - link or source substring: +1 each
102	3. Sorts; takes top-N candidates
103	
104	**Tier 2 — body-grep fallback (slower, ~300ms, auto-fires when tier-1 is insufficient)**
105	
106	Tier-2 re-scores every entity by reading its body file (+2 per topic term present in the body). It fires automatically on **any** of:
107	- tier-1 returned fewer than `--n` matches (too **few** hits), or
108	- **tier-1's best hit is below the confidence floor** (hits too **weak** — default `--tier2-floor 18`), or
109	- `--body-search` is forced.
110	
111	The **confidence gate** (BRO-1426) is the important one: a paraphrase / body-only query used to fill the top-`n` with *weak* distractors, so the old `count < --n` gate never fired and the real (body-only) answer was never surfaced. Now a weak top score (a lone substring/tag hit scores 3–10; a genuine multi-signal match scores ≳ 18) auto-triggers the body read. Calibrated on the 62-query gold-set: it lifts R@5 0.871 → **0.952** and MRR 0.868 → **0.968** *with no flag*, **with 5 gains and 0 per-query regressions** (verified floor 0→18; the body bonus only ever pulled body-only answers into contention, never demoted a tier-1 winner). **Latency note:** because most non-trivial topics have a sub-18 top tier-1 score, tier-2 now fires for the majority of loads — the ~5ms tier-1-only path is the exception (exact-slug/tag hits), the recall-correct default is the ~300ms two-tier pass. Override with `--tier2-floor N` (set `0` to disable the gate; raise it to fire tier-2 more eagerly).
112	
113	This catches entities whose topic vocabulary appears in the prose but not in the dense catalog (claim + tags + slug + links + sources).
114	
115	After scoring, the loader:
116	4. Resolves each top-N entity to its filesystem path via the `path: type/slug.md` field in catalog v2 (eliminates slug-clash ambiguity)
117	5. Reads each entity's full body
118	6. Prints them as one context block
119	
120	### Phase 3 — Reason over loaded context
121	
122	Now the agent has the routing layer (catalog) + the relevant entity bodies in context. Use this for:
123	
124	- **Semantic similarity** — "what other concepts are similar to X?" — the agent reads and compares
125	- **Typed edge inference** — "does X supersede Y?" — read both, infer from prose
126	- **Contradiction detection** — "do any of these entities contradict each other?" — read and judge
127	- **Pattern matching** — "find candidate patterns sourced from a synthesis note that link to active concepts" — read the loaded entities, filter
128	- **Aggregation** — "count entities by status" — agent reads catalog, counts
129	- **Reading frontier** — "given I know X, what should I read next?" — read X's out-edges, prioritize by in-degree
130	
131	### Phase 4 — Persist inferences back to the substrate (binding reflex)
132	
133	Per `AGENTS.md` §P6 sub-rule on substrate-edit-as-inference-persistence: when the agent infers a typed relation from the loaded entities — and the relation is not yet expressed in the substrate — the correct action is to edit the entity's frontmatter `related:` block or body and commit. **Inferences that don't get committed are inferences that didn't happen.**
134	
135	The substrate evolves through reading. A session that loads 20 entities and persists 0 inferences has either genuinely encountered nothing new, or violated the reflex. Both are reportable in the session-close summary.
136	
137	## Output format
138	
139	The skill prints a context block the agent can ingest:
140	
141	```
142	═══ KG LOAD: <topic> ═════════════════════════════════════════
143	
144	Loaded 10/236 entities from docs/knowledge-index.md
145	(catalog generated 2026-05-21T21:53:27+00:00)
146	
147	╭─ #1 · score 28 ──── bstack-engine [pattern·candidate] ──────────╮
148	│ Source: research/entities/pattern/bstack-engine.md              │
149	│ ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── │
150	│ <full entity body>                                              │
151	╰─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
152	
153	╭─ #2 · score 22 ──── recursive-controlled-system [...] ──────────╮
154	│ ...                                                              │
155	╰─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
156	
157	...
158	
159	═══ Total context loaded: 8.3 KB (~2.1k tokens) ════════════════
160	```
161	
162	The bordered blocks make it easy to scan and easy to cite back to disk paths.
163	
164	## Composition with other skills
165	
166	- **ContextSearch** is upstream (PAI session retrieval) — call it for "what did we do" questions; call this skill for "what do we know" questions
167	- **Research** is sideways (web research) — call it for external knowledge; call this skill for internal knowledge
168	- **bookkeeping** is the write side — `bookkeeping run` ingests new material; this skill reads the result
169	- **Knowledge** is the archive — call it for ingestion of long-form content; call this skill for routing within already-ingested material
170	
171	## When NOT to use
172	
173	- **PAI session questions** ("what did we do with X?") — use ContextSearch
174	- **Web research** ("find papers on X") — use Research
175	- **Long-form content ingestion** ("read this 50-page PDF and store it") — use Knowledge ingest
176	- **Single-entity reads when you already know the slug** — just use Read directly on `research/entities/{type}/{slug}.md`
177	- **Catalog generation** — that's `bookkeeping index`, not this skill
178	
179	## Gotchas
180	
181	- **Stale catalog** — if `docs/knowledge-index.md` is >24h old, regenerate via `bookkeeping index` first. The Stop hook does this automatically; if it hasn't fired (e.g., the user has been in a long session), regenerate manually.
182	- **Workspace WIP** — the catalog reflects what's on disk in `research/entities/`, including uncommitted user WIP. That's correct behavior. If validating against committed-only state, regenerate from inside a clean worktree.
183	- **Token budget** — default load is 10 entities (~6-15 KB). Override with `--n` when you need more, but be mindful of context budget for long sessions.
184	
185	## Execution Log
186	
187	After completing any workflow, append a single JSONL entry:
188	
189	```bash
190	echo '{"ts":"'$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)'","skill":"kg","workflow":"load","topic":"<TOPIC>","loaded":"<N>","status":"ok|error","duration_s":<SECONDS>}' >> ~/.claude/PAI/MEMORY/SKILLS/execution.jsonl
191	```

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""
3	kg.py — knowledge graph loader (LLM-as-index routing layer).
4	
5	Reads docs/knowledge-index.md (the dense catalog produced by `bookkeeping index`),
6	ranks entity blocks by topical relevance to a user-supplied topic, and prints
7	the top-N entity bodies as a single context block the agent can ingest.
8	
9	This is the LOAD skill, not a query DSL. Querying is what the agent does
10	once loaded.
11	
12	Architectural anchor: BRO-1223. Substrate is canonical markdown. The agent IS
13	the query engine. No SQLite mirror, no embeddings, no typed-edge schema.
14	
15	Usage:
16	    python3 kg.py load "<topic>" [--n N] [--type T] [--json]
17	                [--terms "a,b"]...   # query expansion (repeatable; one value each)
18	                [--expand 1]         # also load 1-hop related: neighbours
19	                [--explain]          # per-signal score trace
20	    python3 kg.py info                     # catalog stats + top hubs
21	
22	Exit codes:
23	    0  ok
24	    1  no catalog / no matches / user error
25	    2  internal error
26	"""
27	from __future__ import annotations
28	
29	import argparse
30	import json
31	import os
32	import re
33	import sys
34	import time
35	from datetime import datetime, timezone
36	from pathlib import Path
37	
38	# Knowledge-graph paths resolve repo-native + config-driven, defaulting to
39	# today's behavior so the personal ~/broomva graph is unchanged. This mirrors
40	# bookkeeping.py's _resolve_knowledge_paths (the two skills install
41	# independently, so each keeps a self-contained copy). Precedence (highest
42	# first): a TOP-LEVEL `knowledge:` block in the nearest .control/policy.yaml
43	# (found by walking up from CWD; keys root/entities_dir/catalog_path,
44	# root-relative unless absolute) > KG_ROOT/KG_ENTITIES_DIR/KG_CATALOG (legacy
45	# BROOMVA_ROOT still honored for root) > ~/broomva + research/entities +
46	# docs/knowledge-index.md. Only the top-level `knowledge:` key is read — a
47	# nested `plants.knowledge` control-plant block is deliberately ignored.
48	
49	
50	def _find_policy_file(start):
51	    """Nearest-ancestor .control/policy.yaml walking up from `start` (inclusive)."""
52	    start = Path(start).resolve()
53	    for d in (start, *start.parents):
54	        cand = d / ".control" / "policy.yaml"
55	        if cand.is_file():
56	            return cand
57	    return None
58	
59	
60	def _read_knowledge_block(policy):
61	    """Top-level `knowledge:` dict from policy.yaml, or {} if absent/unreadable.
62	
63	    PyYAML is a soft dependency — absent it, returns {} (default resolution).
64	    A missing file, malformed YAML, non-dict root, or non-dict `knowledge:`
65	    all degrade to {}.
66	    """
67	    if policy is None:
68	        return {}
69	    try:
70	        import yaml
71	    except ImportError:
72	        return {}
73	    try:
74	        data = yaml.safe_load(policy.read_text()) or {}
75	    except Exception:
76	        return {}
77	    kn = data.get("knowledge") if isinstance(data, dict) else None
78	    return kn if isinstance(kn, dict) else {}
79	
80	
81	def _abs_or_rel(value, base):
82	    """Expand `value`; return as-is if absolute, else joined under `base`."""
83	    p = Path(value).expanduser()
84	    return p if p.is_absolute() else (base / p)
85	
86	
87	def _resolve_knowledge_paths(start_dir=None, env=None):
88	    """Resolve (root, entities_dir, catalog_path). See precedence comment above.
89	
90	    Pure/testable: `start_dir` defaults to CWD, `env` to os.environ.
91	    """
92	    env = os.environ if env is None else env
93	    start_dir = Path.cwd() if start_dir is None else Path(start_dir)
94	
95	    # (3) default root, honoring legacy BROOMVA_ROOT
96	    root = Path(env.get("BROOMVA_ROOT") or (Path.home() / "broomva")).expanduser()
97	    entities_dir = None
98	    catalog_path = None
99	
100	    # (2) KG_* env overrides (per-key)
101	    if env.get("KG_ROOT"):
102	        root = Path(env["KG_ROOT"]).expanduser()
103	    if env.get("KG_ENTITIES_DIR"):
104	        entities_dir = Path(env["KG_ENTITIES_DIR"]).expanduser()
105	    if env.get("KG_CATALOG"):
106	        catalog_path = Path(env["KG_CATALOG"]).expanduser()
107	
108	    # (1) top-level `knowledge:` block wins (per-key), anchoring root at the repo.
109	    #     KG_NO_POLICY=1 skips this layer entirely — the escape hatch that pins
110	    #     the graph via KG_* env with NO policy override (the bench harness sets
111	    #     it so this loader reads exactly the supplied catalog, even when the CWD
112	    #     walks up into some configured repo).
113	    policy = None if env.get("KG_NO_POLICY") else _find_policy_file(start_dir)
114	    kn = _read_knowledge_block(policy)
115	    if kn and policy is not None:  # non-empty kn implies policy was found
116	        repo_root = policy.parent.parent  # .control/policy.yaml → repo root
117	        # Accept only string path values. A non-str value (YAML coerces
118	        # `entities_dir: yes` → bool, a bare date → date, `123` → int, a list),
119	        # or an unrecognized key, is ignored with a warning — so a mis-authored
120	        # policy DEGRADES to the default rather than crashing every command at
121	        # import time (resolution runs at module load). Honors the
122	        # _read_knowledge_block "degrade to default" contract for bad values too.
123	        for key in kn:
124	            if key not in ("root", "entities_dir", "catalog_path"):
125	                print(f"[kg] ignoring unrecognized knowledge.{key} in {policy}",
126	                      file=sys.stderr)
127	
128	        def _cfg(key):
129	            v = kn.get(key)
130	            if v is None:
131	                return None
132	            if not isinstance(v, str):
133	                print(f"[kg] knowledge.{key} must be a string path (got "
134	                      f"{type(v).__name__}) in {policy}; ignoring", file=sys.stderr)
135	                return None

264	def parse_catalog(text: str) -> tuple[dict, list]:
265	    """Parse the dense catalog into (metadata, [CatalogEntry, ...]).
266	
267	    Supports both schemas:
268	        dense-catalog-v1 (3-line block): header / claim / out·in·tags·src
269	        dense-catalog-v2 (4-line block): + path line, pipe-separated sources
270	
271	    The v2 path line eliminates slug-clash routing ambiguity:
272	    multi-directory slug clashes get a single catalog entry (sorted
273	    last-write wins), and the `path:` field tells the loader exactly
274	    which file that entry describes. Without it, kg.py would rglob and
275	    pick an arbitrary match. With it, load is deterministic.
276	
277	    v2 also pipe-separates sources because moltbook URLs routinely
278	    contain parenthetical commas; comma-splitting fragments ~9% of
279	    sources. The parser handles both `, ` (v1) and ` | ` (v2) for
280	    forward/backward compat — if a `src:` block contains ` | ` it's
281	    v2; otherwise v1.
282	    """
283	    metadata: dict = {}
284	
285	    # Parse YAML frontmatter (between --- markers)
286	    fm_match = re.match(r"^---\s*\n(.*?)\n---\s*\n", text, re.DOTALL)
287	    if fm_match:
288	        for line in fm_match.group(1).splitlines():
289	            if ":" in line:
290	                k, _, v = line.partition(":")
291	                metadata[k.strip()] = v.strip()
292	        text = text[fm_match.end():]
293	
294	    entries: list = []
295	    # Match each entity block: header + claim + meta + optional path
296	    # - score is `[^\n]+?` (rest-of-line, non-greedy) — accepts "7", "7/9",
297	    #   "high", AND space-bearing values like a dict repr ("{'total': '6/9', …}").
298	    #   Defensive: a malformed/space-bearing score must NEVER drop the whole
299	    #   block. The old `\S+` stopped at the first space, so a dict-repr score
300	    #   (emitted by bookkeeping for stub-deterministic entities) made the block
301	    #   fail to match and silently vanish from routing — 23 entities at 370.
302	    #   Root cause is fixed upstream (bookkeeping emits a scalar); this is the
303	    #   belt-and-braces so the loader is robust to any future score shape.
304	    # - meta_line is `[^\n]*` (may be empty for entities without edges/tags)
305	    # - path line is optional (forward-compat with v1 catalogs)
306	    block_re = re.compile(
307	        r"^####\s+(\S+)\s+\[([^\]·]+)·([^\]]+)\](?:\s*·\s*score\s+([^\n]+?))?\s*\n"
308	        r"([^\n]*)\n"
309	        r"([^\n]*)"
310	        r"(?:\npath:\s+(\S+))?\n",
311	        re.MULTILINE,
312	    )
313	
314	    for m in block_re.finditer(text):
315	        slug, type_val, status, score, claim, meta_line, rel_path = m.groups()
316	        e = CatalogEntry(slug.strip())
317	        e.type = type_val.strip()
318	        e.status = status.strip()
319	        # Score kept as string — accepts "7", "7/9", "high", etc.
320	        e.score = score.strip() if score else None
321	        e.claim = claim.strip()
322	        e.rel_path = rel_path.strip() if rel_path else ""
323	        e.raw_block = m.group(0)
324	
325	        # Parse meta_line: → A, B · ← C, D · #tag1 #tag2 · src: source1 | source2
326	        meta_parts = [p.strip() for p in meta_line.split("·")]
327	        for part in meta_parts:
328	            if part.startswith("→ "):
329	                e.out_links = [x.strip() for x in part[2:].split(",") if x.strip()]
330	            elif part.startswith("← "):
331	                e.in_links = [x.strip() for x in part[2:].split(",") if x.strip()]
332	            elif part.startswith("#"):
333	                e.tags = [t.lstrip("#").strip() for t in part.split() if t.startswith("#")]
334	            elif part.startswith("aka: "):
335	                # Alternate names (BRO-1423): comma-separated. Scored like slugs
336	                # so a query for an alias routes to this entity.
337	                e.aliases = [x.strip() for x in part[5:].split(",") if x.strip()]
338	            elif part.startswith("src: "):
339	                src_str = part[5:]
340	                # v2 uses ' | ' separator (robust to commas in source URLs).
341	                # Fall back to ',' for v1 catalogs.
342	                if " | " in src_str:
343	                    e.sources = [x.strip() for x in src_str.split(" | ") if x.strip()]
344	                else:
345	                    e.sources = [x.strip() for x in src_str.split(",") if x.strip()]
346	
347	        entries.append(e)
348	
349	    return metadata, entries

354	def score_entity(entry: "CatalogEntry", topic_terms: list, body_text: str = "",
355	                 trace: "list | None" = None) -> int:
356	    """Score an entity for topical relevance.
357	
358	    Scoring rubric (additive, all case-insensitive):
359	        +10  any topic_term is exactly the slug
360	        +8   any topic_term is exactly an alias (BRO-1423 — an alias is a
361	             deliberate alternate identity, incl. a merged-away dup's slug;
362	             scored just below the slug so querying an alias routes here)
363	        +5   any topic_term is a substring of the slug
364	        +4   any topic_term is a substring of an alias
365	        +4   any topic_term matches a tag exactly
366	        +3   any topic_term is a substring of any tag
367	        +3   any topic_term appears in the claim
368	        +2   any topic_term appears in the body (only checked if body provided)
369	        +1   any topic_term appears in any out_link or in_link slug
370	        +1   any topic_term appears in any source
371	
372	    If `trace` is a list, each contributing signal is appended as a
373	    (label, points) tuple — this powers `--explain` with zero cost on the
374	    hot path (callers that don't explain pass trace=None).
375	    """
376	    score = 0
377	    slug_l = entry.slug.lower()
378	    claim_l = entry.claim.lower()
379	    aliases_l = [a.lower() for a in entry.aliases]
380	    tags_l = [t.lower() for t in entry.tags]
381	    sources_l = [s.lower() for s in entry.sources]
382	    links_l = [s.lower() for s in (entry.out_links + entry.in_links)]
383	    body_l = body_text.lower() if body_text else ""
384	
385	    def _hit(label: str, pts: int) -> None:
386	        nonlocal score
387	        score += pts
388	        if trace is not None:
389	            trace.append((label, pts))
390	
391	    for t in topic_terms:
392	        if t == slug_l:
393	            _hit(f"slug=={t}", 10)
394	        elif t in slug_l:
395	            _hit(f"slug~{t}", 5)
396	
397	        for alias in aliases_l:
398	            if alias == slug_l:
399	                continue  # a self-alias would double-count the slug hit (BRO-1423 review)
400	            if t == alias:
401	                _hit(f"alias=={t}", 8)
402	                break
403	            elif t in alias:
404	                _hit(f"alias~{t}", 4)
405	                break
406	
407	        for tag in tags_l:
408	            if t == tag:
409	                _hit(f"tag=={t}", 4)
410	                break
411	            elif t in tag:
412	                _hit(f"tag~{t}", 3)
413	                break
414	
415	        if t in claim_l:
416	            _hit(f"claim~{t}", 3)
417	
418	        if body_l and t in body_l:
419	            _hit(f"body~{t}", 2)
420	
421	        if any(t in lk for lk in links_l):
422	            _hit(f"link~{t}", 1)
423	
424	        if any(t in s for s in sources_l):
425	            _hit(f"src~{t}", 1)
426	
427	    return score

431	    """Split a topic into searchable terms (lowercase, no punctuation, no stopwords)."""
432	    # Tokenize on whitespace + punctuation, keep underscores

434	    # Drop common english stopwords that add no signal
435	    stopwords = {
436	        "the", "a", "an", "and", "or", "but", "if", "of", "to", "in", "on", "for",
437	        "with", "as", "is", "are", "was", "were", "be", "been", "do", "does", "did",
438	        "from", "by", "at", "what", "how", "why", "when", "where", "all", "any",
439	        "this", "that", "these", "those", "i", "you", "we", "they", "it", "its",
440	        "their", "them", "us", "our",
441	    }
442	    return [t for t in tokens if t not in stopwords and len(t) >= 2]

553	def cmd_load(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
554	    """Load top-N entities for the topic.
555	
556	    Two-tier scoring:
557	      Tier 1 — catalog-only score (claim + tags + slug + links + sources).
558	               Fast (~5ms) and zero filesystem hits beyond the catalog.
559	      Tier 2 — entity-body grep, only triggered when tier 1 returns fewer
560	               than N matches (or --body-search is forced). Slower
561	               (~300ms for ~250 entities) but recovers entities whose
562	               topic appears only in prose, not the dense catalog.
563	
564	    The two-tier approach honors the LLM-as-index architecture: the
565	    catalog routes for terms it knows about; the body grep is the
566	    "load on demand" fallback for terms the catalog can't see.
567	    """
568	    if not args.topic:
569	        print("Usage: kg.py load \"<topic>\" [--n N]", file=sys.stderr)
570	        return 1
571	
572	    if not CATALOG_PATH.exists():
573	        print(f"[kg] catalog not found at {CATALOG_PATH}. "
574	              "Regenerate with: python3 skills/bookkeeping/scripts/bookkeeping.py index",
575	              file=sys.stderr)
576	        return 1
577	
578	    age = time.time() - CATALOG_PATH.stat().st_mtime
579	    if age > STALE_WARN_SECONDS and not args.quiet:
580	        hrs = int(age / 3600)
581	        print(f"[kg] warning: catalog is {hrs}h old. "
582	              "Consider regenerating with `bookkeeping index`.",
583	              file=sys.stderr)
584	
585	    text = CATALOG_PATH.read_text(errors="replace")
586	    metadata, entries = parse_catalog(text)
587	
588	    if not entries:
589	        print(f"[kg] catalog at {CATALOG_PATH} has no parseable entity blocks",
590	              file=sys.stderr)
591	        return 1
592	
593	    if args.type:
594	        entries = [e for e in entries if e.type == args.type]
595	        if not entries:
596	            print(f"[kg] no entities of type '{args.type}' in catalog", file=sys.stderr)
597	            return 1
598	
599	    topic_terms = tokenize_topic(args.topic)
600	    # Query expansion (A): agent-supplied synonym/variant terms are scored
601	    # alongside the topic. The agent is already in the loop, so it IS the
602	    # query expander — QMD fine-tunes a 1.7B model for this only because it
603	    # runs headless. Each --terms value may itself be comma/space separated.
604	    # Dedupe preserving order so the topic's own terms keep priority.
605	    if getattr(args, "terms", None):
606	        for extra in args.terms:
607	            topic_terms.extend(tokenize_topic(extra))
608	        topic_terms = list(dict.fromkeys(topic_terms))
609	    if not topic_terms:
610	        print(f"[kg] topic '{args.topic}' tokenized to nothing meaningful "
611	              "(all stopwords or punctuation)", file=sys.stderr)
612	        return 1
613	
614	    # Tier 1: catalog-only scoring (fast — claim + tags + slug + links + sources)
615	    scored = []
616	    by_slug = {e.slug: e for e in entries}
617	    for e in entries:
618	        s = score_entity(e, topic_terms)
619	        if s > 0:
620	            scored.append((s, e))
621	
622	    # Tier 2: body grep fallback — fires when catalog signal is insufficient.
623	    # Trigger conditions (any):
624	    #   - --body-search flag forces it always
625	    #   - tier 1 returned fewer than args.n matches (too FEW hits)
626	    #   - tier 1's best hit is below the confidence floor (hits too WEAK) — this
627	    #     is the auto-recall gate: a query with ≥n weak distractors used to
628	    #     suppress tier-2 and never surface the body-only answer (BRO-1426).
629	    # Body scoring uses the same rubric as tier 1 but reads file content;
630	    # adds +2 per topic term that appears in the body. Already-scored
631	    # entities accumulate body bonus; new entities enter scored list.
632	    tier1_hits = len(scored)
633	    tier1_top = max((s for s, _ in scored), default=0)
634	    _floor_arg = getattr(args, "tier2_floor", None)
635	    floor = _floor_arg if _floor_arg is not None else TIER2_CONFIDENCE_FLOOR
636	    low_confidence = tier1_top < floor
637	    tier2_added = 0
638	    if args.body_search or tier1_hits < args.n or low_confidence:
639	        slug_to_score = {e.slug: s for s, e in scored}
640	        for e in entries:
641	            # Skip if filesystem path is unknown (catalog v1 entries without path:)
642	            body_path = (ENTITIES_DIR / e.rel_path) if e.rel_path else None
643	            if body_path is None or not body_path.exists():
644	                # Fall back to rglob
645	                candidates = list(ENTITIES_DIR.rglob(f"{e.slug}.md"))
646	                candidates = [p for p in candidates if ".lago-blobs" not in p.parts]
647	                if not candidates:
648	                    continue
649	                body_path = candidates[0]
650	            try:
651	                body = body_path.read_text(errors="replace").lower()
652	            except Exception:
653	                continue
654	            body_bonus = sum(2 for t in topic_terms if t in body)
655	            if body_bonus > 0:
656	                old_score = slug_to_score.get(e.slug, 0)
657	                new_score = old_score + body_bonus
658	                slug_to_score[e.slug] = new_score
659	                if old_score == 0:
660	                    tier2_added += 1
661	        # Rebuild scored list from updated map
662	        scored = [(s, by_slug[slug]) for slug, s in slug_to_score.items() if s > 0]
663	
664	    if not scored:
665	        print(f"[kg] no entities matched topic terms {topic_terms} "
666	              f"(neither catalog nor body)", file=sys.stderr)
667	        return 1
668	
669	    if not args.quiet and tier2_added > 0:
670	        print(f"[kg] tier-2 body search added {tier2_added} entities "
671	              f"(tier-1 catalog scoring found {tier1_hits})", file=sys.stderr)
672	
673	    # Hub-aware tiebreak (D): at equal topical relevance, prefer the more
674	    # central entity (higher catalog in-degree) over arbitrary alphabetical
675	    # order. `in_links` is capped by the catalog preset (top-5 full / top-3
676	    # compact), so this is a capped centrality proxy — enough to beat a pure
677	    # alpha tiebreak and capture most of the value of a hub-rank RRF term.
678	    scored.sort(key=lambda x: (-x[0], -len(x[1].in_links), x[1].slug))
679	    top = scored[: args.n]
680	    score_by_slug = {e.slug: s for s, e in scored}
681	
682	    # Graph 1-hop expansion (B): optionally pull the `related:` neighbours of
683	    # the top hits into the load. This is the structural advantage flat-
684	    # document search engines (QMD, BM25) cannot offer — the agent gets the
685	    # matched entities AND their immediate graph neighbourhood, automating the
686	    # manual "reading frontier" step. Neighbours are deduped against the
687	    # primary set, ranked by their own relevance then in-degree, and capped at
688	    # --n so a hub neighbour (e.g. `arcan`, in-degree 111) cannot explode load.
689	    expansion: list = []  # (seed_slug, entry)
690	    expand_hops = getattr(args, "expand", 0) or 0
691	    # Only 1-hop is supported for now. Each match carries a single `via` (its
692	    # immediate parent); at hop 1 every parent is a primary top-N entity, which
693	    # is always present in the result set, so provenance can never dangle.
694	    # Deeper hops would need full-ancestry tracking + ancestor-preserving caps
695	    # (a capped flat list can keep a deep node while dropping its intermediary)
696	    # — deferred. Clamp values >1 to 1 with a note rather than mislabel depth.
697	    if expand_hops > 1:
698	        if not args.quiet:
699	            print("[kg] note: --expand currently supports a single hop; "
700	                  "clamping to 1.", file=sys.stderr)
701	        expand_hops = 1
702	    if expand_hops > 0:
703	        if args.type and not args.quiet:
704	            # by_slug only holds the type-filtered set, so cross-type related:
705	            # edges (the common case) won't resolve — say so rather than return
706	            # a silently-empty neighbourhood.
707	            print(f"[kg] note: --expand neighbours are limited to type='{args.type}' "
708	                  "(cross-type related: edges aren't resolved under --type)",
709	                  file=sys.stderr)
710	        primary_slugs = {e.slug for _, e in top}
711	        seen_exp: set = set()
712	        frontier = [e for _, e in top]
713	        for _hop in range(expand_hops):
714	            next_frontier = []
715	            for seed in frontier:
716	                for nb_slug in (seed.out_links + seed.in_links):
717	                    nb = by_slug.get(nb_slug)
718	                    if nb is None or nb.slug in primary_slugs or nb.slug in seen_exp:
719	                        continue
720	                    seen_exp.add(nb.slug)
721	                    expansion.append((seed.slug, nb))
722	                    next_frontier.append(nb)
723	            frontier = next_frontier
724	        expansion.sort(key=lambda se: (-score_by_slug.get(se[1].slug, 0),
725	                                       -len(se[1].in_links), se[1].slug))
726	        expansion = expansion[: args.n]
727	
728	    # Phase 2: resolve to filesystem paths.
729	    # Catalog v2 carries explicit `path:` per entity — load that file exactly
730	    # (no rglob ambiguity on slug clashes). Falls back to rglob for v1.
731	    def _resolve_body(e: "CatalogEntry"):
732	        if e.rel_path:
733	            candidate = ENTITIES_DIR / e.rel_path
734	            if candidate.exists():
735	                return candidate
736	        candidates = [p for p in ENTITIES_DIR.rglob(f"{e.slug}.md")
737	                      if ".lago-blobs" not in p.parts]
738	        return candidates[0] if candidates else None
739	
740	    # matches tuple: (relevance_score, entry, body_path, via)
741	    #   via=None        → primary topical match
742	    #   via="<seed>"    → pulled in by --expand as a 1-hop neighbour of <seed>
743	    matches: list = []
744	    for rscore, e in top:
745	        body_path = _resolve_body(e)
746	        if body_path is None:
747	            continue  # Skip entities whose files we can't locate (catalog drift)
748	        matches.append((rscore, e, body_path, None))
749	    for seed_slug, e in expansion:
750	        body_path = _resolve_body(e)
751	        if body_path is None:
752	            continue
753	        matches.append((score_by_slug.get(e.slug, 0), e, body_path, seed_slug))
754	
755	    if not matches:
756	        print(f"[kg] matched {len(top)} entities in catalog but no body files found "
757	              "(catalog may be stale)", file=sys.stderr)
758	        return 1
759	
760	    # --explain (C): compute per-entity catalog-signal traces for the matched
761	    # set only (top-N — cheap). Body-grep bonus shows as a residual line.
762	    explain_traces = None
763	    if getattr(args, "explain", False):
764	        explain_traces = {}
765	        for _rs, e, _bp, _via in matches:
766	            tr: list = []
767	            score_entity(e, topic_terms, trace=tr)
768	            explain_traces[e.slug] = tr
769	
770	    full = not args.no_bodies
771	    if args.json:
772	        print(render_json_output(args.topic, matches, metadata, full_bodies=full))
773	    else:
774	        print(render_load_output(
775	            args.topic, matches, metadata, len(entries), full_bodies=full,
776	            explain_traces=explain_traces,
777	        ))
778	
779	    return 0
780	
781	
782	def cmd_info(_args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
783	    """Print catalog stats + top hubs."""
784	    if not CATALOG_PATH.exists():
785	        print(f"[kg] catalog not found at {CATALOG_PATH}", file=sys.stderr)
786	        return 1
787	
788	    text = CATALOG_PATH.read_text(errors="replace")
789	    metadata, entries = parse_catalog(text)
790	
791	    age = time.time() - CATALOG_PATH.stat().st_mtime
792	    age_h = age / 3600
793	
794	    print(f"Catalog: {_display_path(CATALOG_PATH)}")
795	    print(f"  generated: {metadata.get('generated', '?')}")
796	    print(f"  age:       {age_h:.1f}h")
797	    print(f"  entities:  {len(entries)}")
798	    print(f"  schema:    {metadata.get('schema', '?')}")
799	    print()
800	
801	    # Type breakdown from parsed entries
802	    by_type: dict = {}
803	    for e in entries:
804	        by_type[e.type] = by_type.get(e.type, 0) + 1
805	    print("By type:")
806	    for t in sorted(by_type, key=lambda x: -by_type[x]):
807	        print(f"  {t:24s} {by_type[t]}")
808	    return 0
809	
810	
811	def build_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
812	    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(
813	        prog="kg",
814	        description="Knowledge graph loader (LLM-as-index routing layer)",
815	    )
816	    sub = p.add_subparsers(dest="cmd", required=True)
817	
818	    p_load = sub.add_parser("load", help="Load top-N entities for a topic")
819	    p_load.add_argument("topic", help="Free-form topic to load entities for")
820	    p_load.add_argument("--n", type=int, default=10,
821	                        help="Number of entities to load (default 10)")
822	    p_load.add_argument("--type", help="Restrict to entity type (concept, pattern, …)")
823	    p_load.add_argument("--terms", action="append", metavar="TERM",
824	                        help="Query expansion: extra synonym/variant terms to score "
825	                             "alongside the topic. Repeatable (one value per flag), and "
826	                             "each value may be comma/space-separated "
827	                             "(e.g. --terms 'retrieval,recall').")
828	    p_load.add_argument("--expand", type=int, default=0, metavar="HOPS",
829	                        help="Graph expansion: also load the 1-hop `related:` neighbours "
830	                             "of the top hits (adds up to --n more entities, so total "
831	                             "load is at most 2x--n; values >1 clamp to 1 for now; "
832	                             "default 0 = off).")
833	    p_load.add_argument("--explain", action="store_true",
834	                        help="Show the per-signal score trace for each loaded entity.")
835	    p_load.add_argument("--json", action="store_true", help="Machine-readable output")
836	    p_load.add_argument("--no-bodies", action="store_true",
837	                        help="Skip entity body content (catalog blocks only)")
838	    p_load.add_argument("--body-search", action="store_true",
839	                        help="Force tier-2 entity-body grep. By default tier-2 "
840	                             "auto-fires when tier-1 returns fewer than --n hits OR "
841	                             "its best hit is below the confidence floor; this forces "
842	                             "it unconditionally.")
843	    p_load.add_argument("--tier2-floor", type=int, default=None, metavar="SCORE",
844	                        help=f"Tier-1 top-score below which tier-2 auto-fires "
845	                             f"(default {TIER2_CONFIDENCE_FLOOR}). Set 0 to disable the "
846	                             f"confidence gate (tier-2 then fires only on count<--n).")
847	    p_load.add_argument("--quiet", action="store_true", help="Suppress staleness warnings")
848	    p_load.set_defaults(func=cmd_load)
849	
850	    p_info = sub.add_parser("info", help="Print catalog stats")
851	    p_info.set_defaults(func=cmd_info)
852	
853	    return p
854	
855	
856	def main() -> None:
857	    parser = build_parser()
858	    args = parser.parse_args()
859	    sys.exit(args.func(args))
860	
861	
862	if __name__ == "__main__":
863	    main()
